note: Passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person and nobody may levy a seat, so a toll on it is collectable only where one throne can still say who crosses. The Void Emperor holds the Tier Stair because the stair is the only road in the setting whose position can be described the same way twice, and a tariff no single decider can enforce is a tariff no house will quote.

One recorded pairing was crossed once because passage had become the one controllable supply chain, then repeated until the household no longer surveyed as either race, so four generations have spent themselves correcting one census entry. A crossing that can only be performed where one seat decides who crosses is not a habit, it is a permission, and a permission is inherited with the route rather than with the blood.

A house that publishes credit, safe-conduct and trading posts against exclusivity is enforceable only where a crossing can be refused, so the whole arrangement rests on one office's willingness to close a pier. The Saltledger's exclusivity is a claim about roads and the Void Emperor is the only seat in the setting that can make a road into a fact, which is why the house and the throne need each other and neither can buy the other out.

The network works the tailings on a severed isle nobody collects from and sells the result as spirit stone, so its inventory is whatever the last flood left where it lay. The Void Serpent binds to water that has just gone somewhere else and reads its ground as drainage rather than depth, which makes it the only figure that can say where a bed went after the water left - and that reading is the entire basis of what a residue broker is buying.

The company underwrites a caravan against a road closing because no market can price the risk, and the premium it writes needs something that recurs. On a tier with no season the one cycle anybody can rely on is weather, and the Venom Serpent is the only figure on the plains whose territory is a date rather than a place - it lives in wet ground that exists only during the flood. An underwriter quoting a body's calendar is the closest thing this frame has to a forecast.

The marriages are kept because a merger would make both houses priceable and a priceable counterparty can be bought, and the premium is payable only against something recurring. The Storm Phoenix chronicler keeps the records that were made in weather, which on these plains is the only event that returns on a cycle anybody can rely on, so the indemnity quotes from that record and quotes nothing without it.

A household's standing in the salt dominion is the depth of water it may moor at, and the basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment shrinks without anyone having done anything. Depth is only legible against a mark that stayed while the water moved, and the Skin Tempering Guardian has stood in a flood line for four decades on a tier whose only river relocates its bed once a generation. It is the one figure here that has spent a career learning where the water is not.

The only coastline in the setting that holds its shape is a spirit-tier one, and the Void Leviathan was assembled from the deepest cold water on it - a fact the plains cannot produce at any price. The single piece of evidence that the matching is a property of the water and not of the shore therefore exists only because somebody built a body out of that water and then could not explain why it stopped, which is the whole of the mystery's remaining content.

Ore is the one thing on the plains a core can be caged in, and the work at the face needs a realm the tier does not license, so every body the guild employs is a visitor. The Body of Dao Guardian holds the rung at which a practitioner first carries a place and has left behind patches of ground its own frame will not tolerate leaving; those patches are the only inventory of who has held the quarry face and let it go, and the guild cannot read its own ground without them.

Exactly one account of the ceiling survives, held by a college that will not corroborate it, because corroboration needs a second body. The Adamant Body Guardian's ground has been kept deliberately empty for four decades and the emptiness is the whole of its practice, so the single remaining witness to an unexplained stop at realm seventeen is a figure whose entire method is refusing to have a second body anywhere on the line. That is why the account cannot be checked and has not been replaced.

Every member came from a lineage that stopped one gate short of the ceiling and had no cultivator left to produce, so this household is made entirely of competent strangers. The Body of Immortality Guardian holds its gate on ground that is itself already unproven, on the reasoning that a claim nobody can check has to be held where nobody else can check either, and a pass there is a claim the ground cannot support. That is precisely the qualification this house consists of.

The line guards one founder's forge relic and has refused every offer to sell, lend or exhibit it, because the object that made the ladder climbable is worth more than the ground it stands on. The Iron Titan is the only figure in the setting made entirely of what a mine left behind, and it stands on a heap that has not moved in forty years. A relic nobody will part with is a heap nobody will move, and at this site those are the same object.

Ten seats over six groups leaves four duplicate imprints, and a duplicate has to be carried by somebody, which is why these households hold the Court's second layer with no owner at all. The Body of Unity Guardian holds its gate where several laws are written at once and is the gate the four unfillable seats are quietly made to resemble. The household that carries a duplicate imprint is standing where that resemblance was first demonstrated, which is why the custody has a keeper and no claimant.

Cutting the jade is also grazing the only map of where the seam runs, so any cutting and any map are the same square of earth and the prize was never splittable. The Bone Refining Guardian holds its gate in a pit cut into living stone, because a hollow in unworked rock is the only ground quiet enough to close one in, and it is the only figure on the Cairn Field that was dug rather than appointed. A map that dies under the cut is exactly the argument its excavation makes.

The charter renews on silence and a body that wants the assay figure hidden cannot also be reading the same book, so this conflict is a question about who is permitted an instrument. The Copper Body Guardian does not test a practitioner so much as apply the plains' own law pressure deliberately, from ground where that pressure already runs near its ceiling. Three law slots on a hundred-year body is the whole of what a mortal world does to a person, and this is the gate that makes the world do it on purpose - which is the assay nobody may publish.

The Mortal Plains licenses no humanoid, so every soul inside these walls is a visitor and the garrison is held by people whose trade, family and loyalty are all somewhere else. The Iron Titan is assembled out of the slag of a spent seam and is the only figure here made entirely of what the fort's own predecessors left behind, so the garrison's material and its garrison are the same supply. A wall held by what the last crew could not use is still the only wall on this tier.

A ring marking is a claim that the same body has stood on the same ring across periods, and only one figure on the Cairn Field can support such a claim: the Marrow Cleansing Guardian, which has never been found absent from its ground and is the single continuity the nine gates agree on while disagreeing on everything else. The mark is not a reading of the ring, it is a reading of one body's attendance, and that is a harder thing to fake than an assay.

At a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the frame distinguishes two bodies by a colony that dies. The Iron Sage at the archive keeps whatever is written down on iron-rich worked ground, which on these plains is the only record that has ever survived, because iron outlasts the paper and the paper outlasts the hand. A register that reads the frame instead of the village is exactly as good as the hand it is written by.

The only standing force on the plains exists because the one door out of a world that licenses nobody to enter it fills with unlicensed arrivals, and a queue of bodies is the one thing that must not become a fight. The Iron Body Guardian stands on the heaviest ground the plains has because the ninth gate is the first refusal to break, and a refusal is only credible on a floor that has already refused something. The force that holds the queue is the force that knows what a refusal costs.

Members are entered into the year's dead as one declared group rather than kept on a family roll, because the Cinder Famine made every individual short of fuel and the shortfall collective at once. The Storm Phoenix chronicler keeps the records that were made in weather, and weather is the only event here that recurs on a cycle anybody can rely on. A group entry is a calendar entry, so the household that keeps its dead collectively is kept by the one hand that can date a cycle.

Four immortal and nine transcendent seats stand vacant and no procedure can certify any of them empty, so an unoccupied seat is still a title and the only thing it pays is the cost of being argued about. The Body of Divinity Guardian is the only figure in the setting that has survived being cited, and it has been cited in three separate attempts to fill a vacant seat, each of which failed on the same ground. Nothing here can be inherited, only re-attempted - and that is the estate this line holds.

Partners left behind when the cultivators went up the Tier Stair hold the name of somebody who is not here and refuse to fill the gap, because a name with nobody in it is still a name and a child of the absent must not be counted twice. The Void Serpent holds its ground on the flood line rather than the bank, so its presence is a statement about drainage and not about depth. A household that keeps an absence named is running the same discipline as a binding that reads where the water went.

The last two mortal gates were shut from the inside by the frame, and the people who proved that are the reason anyone now knows the ceiling is a law rather than a defeat. The Muscle Forging Guardian holds the first rung of the Body ladder and is the only gate on the Cairn Field sited for flatness rather than for ore, because a frame has to be set before it can carry anything at all. The era that closed at realm nine is decided at the first rung, and the rung is the only gate whose ground was chosen for the setting rather than the work.

Whether a body may be entered in the register at all cannot be split, because the frame distinguishes the colonized body from the ordinary one by a colony that dies. The Blood Refining Guardian holds the eighth gate on a ring wide and unbroken, since everything a practitioner has taken apart has to be reassembled on one site and a divided ground would let a body be returned in pieces. A colony is a reassembly that happened without a single site, and this is the gate that says so in the only vocabulary the frame has.

One member of each counting house keeps the real figures in their head, unrecorded, because a house that files everything cannot be left alone. The Void Serpent chronicler keeps the records of things that are absent, which the plains can supply honestly and nothing else can. An unrecorded figure and an absent record are the same refusal pointed at numbers and at people, and neither one can be handed to an auditor without dissolving.

A funeral is entered as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, which makes the settlement's dead an inventory rather than a consolation. The Marrow Cleansing Guardian holds the first gate on the ring where something can simply be gone afterwards, and is placed on the most heavily watched ground on the Cairn Field for that reason rather than for difficulty. Burial as inventory is that gate's discipline applied to a village: the question is never who is mourned but whether the body can be accounted for afterwards.

The mortal office certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of the gate fees, and it exists because the tier licenses no humanoid, so a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind here - the reading has to be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. The Copper Body Guardian applies the plains' own law pressure deliberately from ground where that pressure already runs near its ceiling, which makes it the only instrument available to a seat that cannot trust a resident's verdict.

The observation of a strained law only counts if it is repeated, and at this band one repetition costs a lifetime, so the work is done by a very small and very old body. The Body of Transcendence Guardian holds its gate where the ley thins out, on the principle that a frame which has stopped depending on the frame should be tested where there is least left to lean on. It is the only figure on the ring that has moved its own ground, and that transfer is the only recorded instance of a gate changing its own answer - which is the answer this office is paid to repeat.

The one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one was made at a founding generation and never repeated, so the line is unevenly spread and unevenly read and a household holding a thin line cannot spend it twice. The Body of Creation Guardian holds the immortal band's opening gate against the ley beneath the ground because the first immortal frame is earth-shaped, and the cut terraces of the ring exist because that figure needed a floor it could dig. A single crossing is only legible on ground cut for an earth-shaped frame, so this line's uneven spread is a measurement problem before it is a blood one.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said and the famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present, and the prize cannot be split because the register is one book read from the frame while a village that may amend its dead may amend its standing. The Iron Sage at the archive keeps whatever is written down on iron-rich worked ground, which is the only record that has ever survived. Both readings are claims about a hand, and only one hand outlasts the village.

The Quench Order teaches deliberate spending of a furnace and closes permanently the moment the body is lit, and the prize is the Emberblood roster, which cannot be split because a standing order assumes an answer. The Storm Phoenix at the forge ground is a fire built to the shape of a bird out of the only fuel the plains produce, so it is lit once and cannot be relit. A discipline that refuses to answer and a furnace that cannot be relit are the same refusal in doctrine and in hardware.

Surplus law rises off the court's surface and behaves like weather, feeding the ley from below, so the ley and the shelf are one system and the supply line belongs to nobody. The Body of Eternity Guardian holds the endurance gate on the one piece of ground in the immortal tier that nothing has ever broken, and has held it long enough that the ring's own records treat its unbrokenness as the finding rather than the test. One square of ground cannot be both fed from beneath and read from above, and this is the ground whose own unbrokenness is the reading.

Whether absence has a fourth signature turns on what stood where the two dropped departments would have gone, and the record keeps one name because the other two were never written down. The Body of Creation Guardian holds the immortal band's opening gate against the ley beneath the ground rather than the sky above it, which makes it the only figure in the setting positioned at the exact point where a seated element would have registered. The question is therefore not answerable without it and not answerable from it either, which is the honest reason the record is short.

A core has to be caged in something and iron ore on the Mortal Plains is the only dense material in the mortal tier's resource list, so the third gate was a mining problem a long time before it was a spiritual one. The Iron Titan is assembled out of the slag of a spent seam and is the only figure in the setting made entirely of what a mine left behind. The recipe is the standing argument that this body is the cage, constructed out of the seam that ran out paying for it.

The Regent may name a seat and may not take one, because every appointment goes through a trial the Regent cannot judge, which is what stops the highest office from being self-perpetuating. The Body of Destruction Guardian is the only figure at this band that has ever refused a candidate on the grounds that the ground was too sheltered, which makes it the setting's one adversarial examiner rather than a gate. An office forbidden to judge its own appointments needs an examiner who will, and this is the only one here who will.

The academy teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and moving the student somewhere that law is missing, because a spare seat is not capacity for a new path but the only condition under which a law can be studied instead of obeyed. The Body of Origin Guardian holds the gate for a net of causes kept open and stands where the ley lines cross rather than on any one of them, because a network cannot be tested at a point. It is the only figure at this band that publishes what it is looking at, and that publication is the reason its verdicts have never once been disputed.

The form-only reading was recorded as a heresy because nothing in a three-slot frame can test it, and the immortal frame holds four duplicate seats, which is exactly the surplus a diff needs. No result is recorded, and a tested heresy would be a second school competing for the same seats, so the absence of a result is the most stable fact about it. The Body of Immortality Guardian holds its gate on ground that is itself already unproven, on the reasoning that a claim nobody can check must be held where nobody else can check either. The only figure sited on deliberately doubtful ground is the only candidate the test site ever had.

The house publishes teaching and takes discretion in return, so what is done inside is not written down and not repeated, which is the whole of its offer to a counting house. The Iron Sage Disciple works the iron sheets, learns the assay and becomes the first person able to say how much of a record survives a decade; it is lesser because it files rather than keeps, and that distinction is the settlement's entire position. An institution whose product is an unwritten chamber needs the one hand here that measures what a record costs to keep.

The seat's succession is an heir under a charter rather than an appointment, so the vacancy is not an oversight but what is left when an arithmetic decision about money meets an office nobody can fill. The Storm Sovereign holds open ground at the crest of the Cairn Field, which is the only weather cycle the plains has and which is not a season and does not keep to one. The March's other vacancy is the same vacancy with a throne attached: a line that cannot be replenished cannot seat anybody, and the office that survives here is the one whose ground recurs without a date.

The house's real figures live in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, so a raid finds nothing to cite and a counting house finds nothing to seize. The Void Serpent chronicler keeps the records of things that are absent, which is the only category the plains can supply honestly. Both are the same refusal - the head instead of the book - and both are unreadable to the party that most wants them, which is why this house and that archive have never needed to meet.

The Court's second layer is the only place a law is written twice and the second writing wins, and an art that re-masters itself every generation exists so nothing it built survives a composition its makers never saw. The prize was the right to be illegible to a composition, and it cannot be split because an institution whose reading changes each generation cannot witness anything. The Body of Unity Guardian holds its gate where several laws are written at once, which on this tier happens only because ten slots over six groups leaves duplicate imprints - and a duplicate is the only fixed reference the art has left.

The three paths were separated and each handed the tier it already occupied, and the naming read as choice, so for three ages nobody costed what a tier actually cost and the shortest-lived path was given the cheapest frame as though cheapness were its nature. The Storm Phoenix chronicler keeps the records that were made in weather and publishes what recurs. The costing that never happened was the costing of the only cycle in this setting anybody could have written down, which is exactly why the error was invisible for three ages.

The holder sets the price and never the date, because the window belongs to the Tidemark season and its worst hours belong to the swift flock, which is the only arrangement that makes a toll defensible and a timetable not. The Void Emperor holds a seat on the Tier Stair because the stair is the only road whose position can be described the same way twice. One authority owns the road's position and the other owns its hours, and neither can take the other's, which is the whole reason this toll holds at all.

Gate fees are the only tax the plains can actually collect, because no tier in the setting can produce a practitioner of its own and a tier with no local cultivators and no export is sustained entirely by spectators. The Storm Phoenix binds open sky to a rising current and refuses everything else, which on a tier that writes elemental law nowhere at the bottom rung is a binding that never quite takes. The fee is charged for a result the setting cannot manufacture, and the only standing at this field is a binding that openly admits it did not take.

The house publishes credit, safe-conduct and trading posts against exclusivity, which is only enforceable while every member refuses to carry a rival's goods, and its whole asset is that nobody can check the figures. The Iron Sage chronicler keeps whatever is written down on iron-rich worked ground and is this house's standing opponent by name, because iron outlasts the paper. The credit therefore exists only for as long as nobody holding that hand agrees to audit it, which is the condition the house is quietly buying.

Every sworn member of the Iron Vine who holds no office is a Ward, and the office recognises no stat at all, because what the Vine hands out is load and not edge. The Organ Tempering Guardian holds the seventh gate on ground chosen for the void underneath it rather than the stone above it, because the hollowing has to make room before anything can be put in the room, and it is the only gate on the ring whose cost falls on a resource rather than on a body. Load is the only thing this office gives and a void is the only thing that carries it.

The household spends its whole substance on an unwritten discipline and calls the result a road network, because a house publishing exclusivity is enforceable only where a crossing can be refused. The Void Emperor holds a seat on the Tier Stair and already depends on the crossing tariff this family controls. One house holds the roads and one throne can close them, and neither can buy its way out of the arrangement because neither owns the other's asset.

The house holds no jade and owns the workings anyway, because jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, so whoever provisions the cutters owns the cleft more durably than whoever digs it; a title that depends on food outlasts a title that depends on a seam. The Void Leviathan was assembled from the deepest cold water on the only coastline that holds its shape, which is a spirit-tier fact the plains cannot produce. A ration is the durable title on a cutting floor, and this is the one body here carried up a tier on somebody's provisioning.

The mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body while the frames keep producing the record without one. The Void Serpent chronicler keeps the records of things that are absent, already files this register, and is the only person in the setting whose entire practice is holding what is not there. The college pays for the seal and charges for the file, so the ambiguity is its standing revenue and its only reliable keeper.

Three surveys of the same anomaly disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated, because disagreement is what makes a certification necessary, and the anomaly is only measurable as distance - which requires a seated spatial law the parent frame does not have. The Skin Tempering Guardian has stood in a flood line for four decades on a tier whose only river moves its bed once a generation. It is the one figure here that has spent a career establishing where the water is not, which is why the disagreement is legible instead of averaged away.

The toll is paid in grain because a toll denominated in the payer's own crop cannot be inflated by the collector, and the useful service is re-finding the crossing rather than maintaining it, since the Widow Run moves its bed far enough to relocate every settlement on it. The Venom Serpent lives in wet ground that exists only during the flood, so its range is measured in weeks a year. Re-finding a crossing once a generation is not a service anybody can schedule, so the figure that knows where the water went is what the toll is actually paying for.

A severed frame keeps paying upkeep that nobody collects and the tailings on it are worth nothing where they lie and unmatchable ashore, so two sellers of the same tailings would make the claim read as invented and the prize cannot be split. The Silver Body Guardian holds the spirit band's second gate on the quarry floor rather than the ridge above it, because the first reservoir fills fastest where ambient qi is already dense and density is measured in cut lengths per unit of ground worked. It stands on the one institution that measures a world instead of praising it, and it is the reason one collector stays solvent.

An indemnity needs a stated exposure and the mutual society's protection is that it states nothing, so computing the premium dissolves the arrangement being insured. The Iron Monarch holds the only worked ground on the plains that has a wall on it, which is the last standing face of a seam that stopped paying forty years ago, and its claim is therefore a claim to a ruin. The house that would have to state the figure is the one whose entire asset is that it cannot be valued, which is why the premium stays unquoted.

A law's tier list says where it may apply while a seat says where it is actually installed, so a law can apply to a tier and still have no seat in it, and the survey is the whole of the Law Census. The Iron Sage chronicler keeps whatever is written down on iron-rich worked ground, which is the only record that has ever survived. The instrument is therefore a count of seats and not a count of bodies - which is the entire reason mortals live under three of six laws without ever knowing three were missing.

The Watchgate brokers sell standing at the Cairn Field on the ground that no tier can produce a practitioner of its own, so gate fees are the only tax the plains can collect, and the whole trade rests on a rumour about who seated which ring. The Storm Sovereign holds open ground at the crest of that field, which is the only weather cycle the plains has and which is not a season and does not keep to one. The rumour is worth standing there for and the standing is worth nothing without the rumour, and neither half of that loop can be audited by anyone standing outside it.

Everyone who is sworn and holds no office sits at this open door in all but name, and it recognises nothing at all, because recognition begins where office begins. It is the one office in the setting whose standing a body does not have to prove, and the Void Serpent's own claim on the plains is drainage rather than depth - a statement about where the water went that requires no reading of the holder at all. An institution whose entire offer is an unearned place is the only one here that a body nothing can scan could accept without being measured first.

Gate fees are the only tax the plains can collect, and the brokers sell standing on the promise that someone once sat a ring and can be asked about it. The Iron Monarch holds the only worked ground on the plains with a wall on it, which is the last standing face of a seam that stopped paying forty years ago, so its claim is a claim to a ruin. That makes it the one piece of standing in this setting held against something already spent, and the only standing a broker can resell without a body ever having to be shown.

This is the other half of the same absence, holding the crop the departed left a claim to instead of the departed's name, because a household with no cultivator still has an estate and grain is the only thing anybody will accept as payment for a crossing. The Venom Serpent's territory is a date rather than a place, so its range is a set of weeks a year. A household that collects in grain along a river that relocates its own bed has to know when the water is gone, and that is the only calendar such a house keeps.

Succession is agreed in a room and never written, because a family that cannot publish a roll cannot inherit by one either, and pressure from a counting house that answers a carriage trade with its own prices produced the most careful paperless practice in the setting. The Void Serpent chronicler keeps the records of things that are absent, which is the only category the plains can supply honestly. A line that keeps its own succession unwritten still has to be legible to somebody, and that somebody is the one hand whose trade is filing what is not there.

The prize is the right to stand on a household roster and it cannot be split, because a roster is a single list and the whole discipline it exists for is reading a person - so a body nothing can inspect is either on the list or the list has stopped meaning anything. The Blood Refining Guardian holds the eighth gate on a ring wide and unbroken, because everything a practitioner has taken apart has to be reassembled on one site and a divided ground would let a body be returned in pieces. Reassembly is the only reading this frame can perform, and it is a reading.

A split tally has two halves and one meaning, reproducible only by two people who were both present, while a credential cloth has one visible fact and no meaning, so a crossing that accepts both cannot afterwards say which one it enforced. The Storm Phoenix chronicler keeps the records that were made in weather and knows the Tidemark the livery is scheduled against. The meaning of a tally lives in two hands that were at the pier, and a culture that identifies a traveller by cloth alone has decided not to count them.

The only exact record below the spirit peaks carries sixty years as a summary instead of entry by entry, in a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate, and the gap is kept legible rather than filled because a filled gap would be an admission. The Iron Sage Disciple is the first person able to say how much of a record survives a decade, and it is lesser because it files rather than keeps. A sixty-year summary is unreadable to anyone who was not there, and the only hand that could expand it maintains records rather than making them.

Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing - all of it produced by pressure from a counting house that answers a carriage trade with prices at its own rates. The Void Serpent chronicler keeps the records of things that are absent and is this culture's natural opposite. The Unfiled exists because the ledger wanted an enumeration, and it holds together against the one hand in the setting whose profession is knowing what is missing - which is why the two have never needed to meet.

Realms one and two, in a tier that seats three of the six laws, and it starts as a fuel-rationing problem because qi law bottoms out at 0.1, so a mortal world carries roughly enough qi to light a first breath and none to spare. The Muscle Forging Guardian holds the first rung of the Body ladder and is the only gate on the Cairn Field sited for flatness rather than for ore, because a frame has to be set before it can carry anything at all. The first breath is a setting problem and the first rung is where it is solved, on ground chosen for the setting rather than for the work.

The office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, because four vacant seats were very nearly filled by decree and that attempt taught this setting to write a vacancy as its own state rather than as a zero. The Void Serpent chronicler keeps the records of things that are absent, already holds a place in this office, and already keeps the register of unopened coffins. A vacancy is only writable as its own state if somebody is professionally responsible for absence, and this is that hand.

A frame raised its physical law to make material harder and every existing body failed in one night, so the only copy of how to stop it happening died with the people who had it, and no glasskin has been born since. The Body of the Dao Guardian holds the last rung of the Body ladder on ground that is itself a broken law and has not finished curing, and it is the setting's clearest case of a test that is hostile to the frame. The method is a way of stopping a law from finishing, and the only figure still standing on unfinished law is the one that could have written it down.

Ore is the one thing on the plains a core can be caged in and the work at the face needs a realm the tier does not license, so every body the guild employs is a visitor. The Silver Body Guardian holds the spirit band's second gate on the quarry floor rather than the ridge above it, because the first reservoir fills fastest where ambient qi is already dense and density is measured in cut lengths per unit of ground worked. It stands on the one institution in the setting that measures a world instead of praising it, and it is measuring the only dense material this guild has to sell.

The households that were working the seam when it ran out now hold the worked-out face as a title, because honouring a dead claim is cheaper than paying a living one and the grief became an estate. The Iron Monarch holds the only worked ground on the plains that has a wall on it, which is the last standing face of that same seam, and its claim is therefore a claim to a ruin. The grief became inheritable because somebody was still standing on the last face of it, and that is the only Iron Monarch this record holds.

The famine took the people who could have borne children, so the fertile years are empty and the dependents are full, and the line was formed by adoption because the households that survived had none of their own to lose. The Storm Phoenix at the forge ground is a fire built to the shape of one out of the only fuel the plains produce, which is hot worked ground. An adoptive line needs a body to adopt and a household to put it in, and this is the only forge here that produces a body nobody has to be born into.

A body arriving where a required law group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed, so the lodge sells only bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, and a body tuned for a collapsed frame cannot be retuned on the far side. The Body of Humanity Guardian holds the first gate on the Fragmentshelf, where the ground is a broken law, and it is the only figure in the setting that has never been described by a resident of any tier below the top one. It reads rather than strikes, and the only thing worse than an untuned body is a body tuned by a reader.

A fire-affinity culture keeps no museum, because a great ascension is a furnace body opened on purpose, so it keeps an unbroken shell and the whole recovery written down in public with the fragments never displayed again; the register is the relic. The Iron Sage chronicler keeps whatever is written down on iron-rich worked ground and is the archive hand this register is written by. The register's guarantee is publication and the rival guild's is that publication does not survive, so the entire dispute is about whose hand is durable.

Two frames write one group at one value, nothing has crossed in either direction, and every crossing in the setting shares a group with a live neighbour, so if adjacency is as cheap as the rule says then the crossing tariff is a tax on nothing. The Skin Tempering Guardian has stood in a flood line for four decades on a tier whose only river moves its bed once a generation. It is the one figure here whose ground is unreliable by design, which is the only reason anybody would still be watching a boundary that two frames agree about.

A dao fragment cures as it decays and a cured fragment is void crystal, so the shelf is the only resource in the setting that is worthless before its owner is, which makes holding it without a buyer a liability and holding it with one a race. The Body of Humanity Guardian holds the first gate on that shelf, where the ground is itself a broken law. Holding a claim whose value is still curing requires a figure standing on ground that is also still curing, and this is the only one in the setting standing on it.
